clue.text: Little mite smuggled aboard ship doesn't go away

indicators.note: something smuggled aboard is carried hidden within the vessel, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a tick is a tiny mite-like parasite

explanation.surface: A tiny stowaway on board a vessel refuses to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, the usual crossword steamship, is the ship that the little mite boards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to remain in place, so something that sticks stays put.

clue.text: That group shows spirit, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for spirit is shifted to the end

parts.note: ethos is the characteristic spirit of a group or culture

explanation.surface: A team displays real esprit, from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' looks like 'throughout' but tells you to move the E of ETHOS to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural demonstrative pronoun points to a set of things, a group referred to as that.

clue.text: Fellows who may shoot others without killing them

definitions.text: Fellows who may shoot others without killing them

parts.words: Fellows who may shoot others without killing them
parts.note: shoot here means film or photograph, so these men point lenses, not guns, at people

explanation.surface: Men who fire at people yet leave them unharmed sound like poor marksmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests guns; the shooting is filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators of film or television cameras shoot footage of their subjects.

clue.text: Dog in sofa, not quite right

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a settee is a sofa

explanation.surface: A dog lying on the couch isn't really proper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts a dog on the couch, but 'in' is only a link; 'not quite' clips the sofa word to SETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gundog, such as the Irish setter.

clue.text: Platforms allowing vocal quartet to be heard

indicators.note: being heard means the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: the Four Tops were a famous Motown vocal group of four singers

explanation.surface: Stages are set up so a singing foursome can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Four Tops were a Motown vocal quartet; their name, said, gives a nautical word.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship a foretop is the platform at the head of the foremast.

clue.text: Human right that could result in cheeps

parts.note: the word speech, set free to rearrange, makes the word cheeps

explanation.surface: A basic liberty that might lead to birds twittering.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'freedom' is an anagram signal and SPEECH, freed, can give CHEEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Free expression of opinion is counted among the basic liberties all people hold.

clue.text: Wicked hustlers showing no mercy

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters are twisted and corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Evil con artists are merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like a description of the hustlers but signals rearranging HUSTLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pitiless or merciless is the plain synonym of the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Young fellow requesting extra dance

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the orphan in Dickens's novel, famously asks for more gruel
a rock-and-roll dance craze of the early 1960s

explanation.surface: A boy asks for another turn on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan who says 'Please, sir, I want some more'.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Dickens's orphan is also the name of a 1960s gyrating dance.

clue.text: I have a chair, I declare

definitions.meaning: a university chair is a senior academic post held by a top academic
one who declares or avows something openly is one who professes

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they own a seat, or simply proclaiming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' is the academic post, not furniture; and one who professes is, literally, a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a university chair is a senior academic; anyone who avows a belief also professes it.

clue.text: Dedication of US university evident in discussion

indicators.note: something evident in a thing shows up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: comment is remarks or discussion about something
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An American college's commitment shows through in debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedication to a cause is a strong pledge or devotion to it.

clue.text: Endless sarcasm offered by good conductor

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: irony is mocking, sarcastic language

explanation.surface: A fine orchestral conductor gives out unending sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is a conductor of heat and electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: This metal readily carries heat and electric current, so physics calls it a good conductor.

clue.text: Support fire damaged in arch

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bend is a curve or arch

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Holding up an archway that the fire has harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns FIRE into FRIE, which goes 'in' BEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to help and stand by them, offering support.

clue.text: Shiny stuff — no good — rubbish!

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: glitter is sparkly decorative material

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses sparkly decorations as worthless junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' reads as a verdict, but it says remove G from GLITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is waste scattered about, a synonym of rubbish as a noun.

clue.text: Second character surviving flood is a fraud

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's sons, who survived the Flood in the ark

explanation.surface: The other figure who lived through a deluge turns out to be an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth were saved from the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake or impostor, something not genuine.

clue.text: Old listing of characters involved in apartheid

indicators.note: the letters of the word are involved, or tangled, to make something new

explanation.surface: A historic register of people caught up in South Africa's segregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters, here jumbled from APARTHEID.
explanation.definitionFit: The record chart of best-selling songs is a dated term for the pop music listing.

clue.text: Most untidy place for eating that is on street

parts.note: a mess is a military dining hall
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: The scruffiest diner is the one on the high road.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of messy describes the most disordered or untidy.

clue.text: Confession of someone in a hurry was breathtaking?

definitions.text: Confession of someone in a hurry
definitions.meaning: a rushed person admits they are short of time
something breathtaking made a strong mark on people; the question mark flags the loose fit

explanation.surface: A rushed person's admission was apparently stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PRESSED it is a busy person's admission; whole, it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a powerful impression is to amaze, so the past tense matches a stunning effect.

clue.text: Bewildered prisoner mingled

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
fused means melded or blended together

explanation.surface: A dazed inmate mixed with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puzzled and perplexed is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Rugby player Don played in teachers' team maybe

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a school's staff is its team of teachers, one example of a staff

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby man called Don turned out for the teachers' side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' makes DON into NDO, put 'in' STAFF. The stand-off is the fly-half position in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, the stand-off half is the player between scrum-half and the backs, also called fly-half.

clue.text: What is expected by end of week is place in which to relax

parts.note: par is the expected or normal standard, as in golf

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: By the weekend's close, normal routine gives way to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A public green space is where people stroll and unwind.

clue.text: Parts of document getting left out — the reasons?

indicators.note: left out means removed, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: clauses are sections of a legal document

explanation.surface: Sections of a contract were omitted, and someone asks why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting left out' reads as an omission; it says take L from CLAUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Causes are the grounds or motives behind something, plural like the reasons.

clue.text: Duty of a queen intervening in row

indicators.note: something intervening comes between, so it is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
R abbreviates Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch has an obligation to step into a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is pronounced to rhyme with 'cow', a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty can be a tax on imports, which is what a customs schedule lists.

clue.text: Pouring rain'd come from me?

indicators.note: pouring suggests the letters flow out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A god wonders whether the downpour comes from him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Indra is the Hindu god of rain and storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Vedic deity of thunder and rain, the source of downpours.

clue.text: Situation with inadequate leader: such will be ineffective

parts.note: a place is a situation or position

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a boss is a leader

explanation.surface: A post with a feeble manager is doomed to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts BOSS to BOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy pills given in trials have no active ingredient, so they are designed to do nothing.

clue.text: Old chaps beginning to see warning signs

parts.note: men are chaps

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Elderly gents start to notice signs of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are signs foretelling events, often a caution of trouble ahead.

clue.text: Girl? One may be hugged by mother returning

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so one piece goes within the other
returning means the word for mother is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of animals
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A daughter might be embraced by her mum on coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DAM into MAD, which hugs I.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is an old word for a girl or young unmarried woman; the question mark marks the dated sense.

clue.text: Family member tries changing by incremental amounts

parts.note: steps are stages or small increments

indicators.note: changing the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A relative attempts to alter things a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by incremental amounts' reads as describing how the change happens, but it is the first piece; 'changing' rearranges the letters of 'tries' as ISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of one's step-parent is a relative by marriage within a family.

clue.text: Raven had to fly around terrace

indicators.note: letters flying around scatter and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A black bird must flap about the patio.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed platform along a house's side is a kind of terrace or porch.

clue.text: Cruelty making one unhappy is last thing kingdom needs

parts.note: sad means unhappy
I is the Roman numeral for one
is shortens to 's, as in it's

indicators.note: the last thing in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Making someone miserable is the final thing a realm requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives S, as in the contraction 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain on others is a form of cruelty.
